kicker: Paint with code, and its rubric

scenes.headline: How a language model learns to paint in code
scenes.sub: A reasoning model writes p5.brush sketches; a judge scores each render.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Barley! Here a reasoning model learns to paint by writing code. Here's how, and why its first reward got stuck.

scenes.text: Paint by writing p5.brush code, and reward it with a relative question: is this better than two paintings from a hand-rated pool?
scenes.say: The idea: paint by writing code, then reward it with a relative question. Is this painting better than two from a hand-rated pool?

steps.say: A prompt goes to the policy, a reasoning model, which writes a complete p5.brush sketch. The painting is source code.
A sandboxed headless browser runs it and renders the canvas.
A separate judge model compares the image against paintings from a reference pool.
GRPO ranks the rollouts within each group, and updates the policy.

scenes.title: Nine signals, one opinion
scenes.say: The first reward summed nine signals, stalled at point six five, and painted the same clip-art flower every time. Why?

parts.say: correlated point eight five to point nine five with each other,
are worth about one independent opinion. Five API bills, one opinion.

left.title: Score it 0 to 10
items: Scores came back compressed near zero
Tied pairs give GRPO nothing to rank
left.say: Asked for a score out of ten, the judge's marks bunched near zero, and tied pairs teach GRPO nothing.

right.title: Which one is better?
items: The rollout against two pool paintings
Three levels that actually track quality
right.say: Asked which of three is better, it answers reliably. Only three reward levels, but they rank the group.

items.say: Start by rating one thousand six hundred and sixty-four generated paintings by hand.
Against only the best, a young policy loses every comparison, and the gradient goes flat.
So the pool keeps okay paintings too: opponents where losing still teaches.

scenes.text: The correction is not more judges. Count how many independent opinions a rubric holds before you trust its sum.

recap: The painting is code: write, render, judge
Five correlated judges were one opinion
Pairwise questions against a graded pool keep the gradient
scenes.say: To recap: paint in code, count your independent judges, and compare against a pool you can still lose to.
